Notes.Text: These are all security issues fixed in the python313-social-auth-core-7.2.0-1.1 package on the GA media of openSUSE Tumbleweed.
Notes.Title: Details

Vulnerabilities.Description: Python Social Auth is a social authentication and registration mechanism. Prior to 6.2.0, OpenIdConnectAuth in social_core/backends/open_id_connect.py uses get_and_store_nonce to place the OpenID Connect nonce in a shared OpenIdConnectAssociation table, and get_nonce and validate_claims verify only that the nonce exists and has not expired rather than binding it to the browser session and OAuth state that initiated the login. An attacker who obtains a victim's unused authorization code can start a separate login to obtain valid state for the attacker's browser, submit the victim's code with that state, and pass nonce validation because the victim nonce is globally available. With DEFAULT_USE_PKCE disabled in the default OpenIdConnectAuth configuration, the attacker can be logged in as the victim. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.0.

Social-auth-core 4.7.0 before 7.0.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the SAML backend that restores sessions named in the unsigned RelayState parameter. Attackers can deliver their own valid IdP response and RelayState to a victim's browser via an auto-submitting form, signing the victim into the attacker's account to capture entered data.
